Bring a checked keyword sheet back into the data

Source: R/keywords_clean.R
keywords_merge.Rd

Applies the sheet that [keywords_clean()] wrote with `level = "all"`, after it was checked outside R, and returns the data frame. The confirmed steps of [keywords_clean()] are applied again, then the sheet, read one of two ways:

* `by = "merge"` (default), for a person or a model that adds a column `merge` and answers `yes` or `no` in it: * `yes`: the keyword becomes its `name`; * `no`: the keyword keeps its own spelling, also where cleaning had merged it (a `confirmed` row); * empty: what cleaning does stands.

`status` is not read, so a tool that overwrites it (an LLM run log writing `success` on every row) changes nothing, and rows without a `keyword` or `name`, such as a prompt pasted under the table, are skipped. * `by = "edit"`, for a tool that rewrites the keywords themselves, such as OpenRefine clustering the `keyword` column: every keyword whose `keyword` no longer equals its untouched `keyword_backup` becomes the new text. An edited `confirmed` row moves only that spelling; any other edited keyword moves with all its spellings. `merge` and `name` are ignored, and an edit of case or spacing alone changes nothing.

Rows are matched on `keyword_backup` (on `keyword` when a sheet has no backup column with `by = "merge"`). Pass the same `columns` and `replace` as to [keywords_clean()], and the data as it was before cleaning: a confirmed merge marked `no` can only be undone from there (on cleaned data everything else gives the same result).

Usage

keywords_merge(
  data,
  decisions,
  by = c("merge", "edit"),
  columns = "DE",
  replace = NULL,
  output = c("minimal", "all")
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per paper.

decisions

The checked sheet: a data frame (as read with `rio::import()` or `readxl::read_excel()`) or the path of the `.xlsx` or `.csv` file.

by

`"merge"` (default) reads the `merge` column; `"edit"` reads the edits of `keyword` against `keyword_backup`. See above.

columns, replace, output

As in [keywords_clean()].

Value

`data`, same class, rows and columns, with the keyword columns rewritten where they change; with `output = "all"`, plus the `_ORIGINAL` columns. A message reports the counts per column and the rows applied from the sheet.

Errors

Raises `saqrmisc_bad_input` for a missing sheet; with `by = "merge"`, one without `name`, `merge` and `keyword_backup` (or `keyword`), or a `merge` other than empty, `yes` or `no`; with `by = "edit"`, one without `keyword` and `keyword_backup`; and the errors of [keywords_clean()].

See also

[keywords_clean()]

Examples

papers <- data.frame(
  TI = c("Chatbots in class", "Bots that talk", "Fairness at work", "Unfair bosses"),
  DE = c("CHATBOT; NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING (NLP)", "CHAT-BOTS; NLP",
         "INTERPERSONAL JUSTICE", "INTERPERSONAL INJUSTICE; NLP")
)
sheet <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
cleaned <- keywords_clean(papers, level = "all", decisions = sheet, min_papers = 1)
#> file1ff65cc62f29.csv: 3 groups and single keywords, 1 confirmed merges and 2 to check, keywords in 1 or more papers. Nothing is merged yet: add a column `merge` (yes or no), then keywords_merge(data, decisions = "file1ff65cc62f29.csv"). A prompt for a model is in file1ff65cc62f29_prompt.txt.
checked <- utils::read.csv(sheet)
checked$merge <- ifelse(checked$keyword == "NLP", "yes", "no")
utils::write.csv(checked, sheet, row.names = FALSE)
keywords_merge(papers, decisions = sheet)
#> keywords: DE: 6 written forms became 5 keywords; 3 papers changed
#> keywords_merge: from file1ff65cc62f29.csv, 1 keyword(s) marked yes merged into their name, 2 marked no kept apart
#>                  TI                                                   DE
#> 1 Chatbots in class                 CHATBOT; NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING
#> 2    Bots that talk               CHAT-BOTS; NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING
#> 3  Fairness at work                                INTERPERSONAL JUSTICE
#> 4     Unfair bosses INTERPERSONAL INJUSTICE; NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING

# The same sheet edited the way OpenRefine edits it: keyword rewritten,
# keyword_backup untouched.
edited <- utils::read.csv(sheet)
edited$keyword[edited$keyword == "NLP"] <- "NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING"
utils::write.csv(edited, sheet, row.names = FALSE)
keywords_merge(papers, decisions = sheet, by = "edit")
#> keywords: DE: 6 written forms became 4 keywords; 3 papers changed
#> keywords_merge: from file1ff65cc62f29.csv, 1 edited keyword(s) applied, 0 to a spelling not in the data
#>                  TI                                                   DE
#> 1 Chatbots in class                 CHATBOT; NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING
#> 2    Bots that talk                 CHATBOT; NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING
#> 3  Fairness at work                                INTERPERSONAL JUSTICE
#> 4     Unfair bosses INTERPERSONAL INJUSTICE; NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING
